title: Noisy warmup signal caused HPA/KEDA underprovisioning; debounce + guardrails
creator: Priya Shah
description: Summary: During a capacity event on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated underprovisioning where KEDA-triggered scaledowns overlapped with HPA latency signals, producing a cascade of cold-starts and elevated tail latency. This ticket captures investigation notes, the identified root causes (noisy warmup signal from readiness probes + percentile misalignment between KEDA and HPA), and proposed guardrails: probabilistic debounce, weighted warm-pool health signals, and a circuit-breaker to prevent aggressive scaledown when synthetic warmup traffic fails. The goal is to prevent false negatives/positives in scaling decisions while preserving cost controls.
impact: Multiple hosted and Dedicated customers experienced transient 3-6x increase in tail latency and a 10-25% spike in 5xx rates for 12-45 minutes during peak burst windows. Customer-facing SLAs were not violated for all tenants, but internal SLOs for p99 latency were breached for several routes. Business risk: medium-high; operational load during incident: on-call and infra teams for 2.5 hours.
timeline: 2026-03-09T03:12Z - Surge begins: sudden traffic spike on chat-generation routes in us-west-2
2026-03-09T03:17Z - KEDA scales up based on Redis queue length, then begins scaling down within 4 minutes due to short tail pulses
2026-03-09T03:25Z - HPA observes increased 95th/99th latency and triggers extra replicas; however, KEDA scale-downs continued leading to churn
2026-03-09T03:40Z - Multiple cold-starts observed as hot replicas were evicted; p99 latency spikes persisted
2026-03-09T04:10Z - Mitigations applied (manual warm-pool pinning + temporary HPA min increase); latency stabilized by 04:30Z
2026-03-10 - Investigation kickoff; collected metrics, probe traces, and Redis scaler logs
detection: Triggered by automated p99 latency alerting (console-alerts route:chat-gen-p99) and customer escalations. Alert correlated with KEDA controller events and rapid replica churn logs in the serving clusters.
root_cause: Noisy readiness/probe signals: readiness probe latency spikes (caused by GC pauses on a subset of inference workers) were surface as availability blips, which were treated by KEDA/HPA as transient unhealthy signals.

Percentile misalignment: KEDA uses queue-length percentiles across namespaces with a 1m window; HPA uses pod-level p95/p99 latency with a different window. The two windows produced conflicting actions during short bursts.

Aggressive scaledown policy: KEDA configured with aggressive inactivity timeout (30s) and HPA configured to react quickly to latency without backoff, leading to oscillation and cold-start amplification.
Missing warm-pool weighting: warm-pool health checks were not factored into scale-down decisions, so a healthy warm pool did not prevent scaledown when probe flapping occurred on serving pods.
Insufficient synthetic warmup: warm-pool verification relied on production traffic only; when customer traffic pattern changed, warm pool was not exercised and considered idle by autoscalers.
mitigation: Emergency: increased HPA min replicas for affected clusters and added a short-lived annotation to disable aggressive KEDA scale-downs for the burst window (applied 2026-03-09 04:12Z)
Rolled out a temporary probe debounce patch on the readiness probe path to ignore sub-200ms blips (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8721)
Added a synthetic warmup job to exercise warm-pool instances every 45s in high-traffic routes to keep warm-pool seen as active
action_items: AI-1: Implement probabilistic debounce for readiness probes at the controller level (owner: Ethan Kim, due: 2026-03-21) - reduces sensitivity to transient BLIP signals
AI-2: Align percentile windows between KEDA and HPA or introduce cross-check policy that requires agreement across both before scale-down (owner: Maya Lopez, due: 2026-04-01)
AI-3: Introduce 'warm-pool weight' that biases scale-down metrics when warm-pool is healthy (owner: Owen Zhang, due: 2026-03-28)
AI-4: Add a circuit-breaker that prevents KEDA from scaling below a cluster-floor when synthetic warmup jobs fail N times in T minutes (owner: Priya Shah, due: 2026-03-24)

AI-5: Dashboard + alerting: create a composite view (KEDA events, HPA events, probe flaps, warm-pool activity) and add SLO-aware alerts to detect oscillation early (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-18)
AI-6: Run a chaos test that injects GC pauses and probe flaps to measure autoscaler behavior before rolling changes (owner: Reliability Eng, due: 2026-04-08)
AI-7: Update runbook: include steps to pin warm-pool, disable KEDA scale-down, and inspect probe latency traces (owner: On-call docs, due: 2026-03-15)
follow_up: Post-change measurement: Collect 2 weeks of autoscaler telemetry after deploying debounce + warm-pool weight and compare oscillation frequency to baseline
Customer outreach: notify Dedicated customers in affected regions of changes and provide mitigation checklist; include suggested config for tenant-specific min replicas
Consider product-level guardrail: default a conservative scale-down timeout for new clusters until warm-pool synthetic checks are enabled
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Initial triage completed. Collected pod-level probe traces, KEDA scaler logs, and Redis queue histograms. Noticed probe blips coincide with GC events on a small subset of pods.
2026-03-11 Ethan Kim: Reproduced probe flapping locally by inducing 200-400ms GC pauses in a canary cluster. Confirmed that KEDA scales down aggressively despite warm-pool presence.

2026-03-12 Maya Lopez (PM): Reviewed trade-offs. Aggressive scale-down reduces cost but increases risk for bursty workloads. PMs recommend a conservative default and customer opt-in for aggressive config.
2026-03-13 Design review (Liam O'Connor): Suggested UX affordance in Console to visualize cross-oscillation signals and to allow one-click pinning of warm-pools for a tenant.
2026-03-14 Observability lead (Ava Martinez): Drafted dashboard layout and added composite alert prototype to PagerDuty rules. Requesting review from reliability team before turning on globally.
